html:
The American University of Beirut was founded in 1866 by American Protestant missionaries as the Syrian Protestant College. It took its present name in 1920.

It first taught in Arabic and was part of the Nahda, the Arab cultural revival of the late 1800s. Its medical school and its graduates spread across the Middle East. In the 1900s it became a hothouse of Arab nationalism, and many of the leaders, doctors and engineers of the Arab states studied there.

The university kept working through the civil war, although its president Malcolm Kerr was murdered on campus in 1984. With its hospital, it is still one of the leading universities of the region. See also Beirut and Lebanon.
